answer: After every storm the route keeper rebuilds the cairns along the trail and files the survey, and no caravan may travel a route whose cairns are down. A vine cairn stacked in an afternoon fails the survey: at the yarrow of the dune the stones must weather as the file describes, and a fresh pile points travellers toward a dry well. Faking the survey means walking the route for three storm seasons, rebuilding 90 cairns and paying 6,300, while the saffron count in the keeper's file is checked by every guide, so a cairn whose stones were never surveyed is pulled down.
